newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, JAN 13-SUNDAY, JAN 19.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, JAN 13-SUNDAY, JAN 19.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
BRUSSELS - European Commissioners Brittan, van den Broek and Van Miert meet Japanese International Trade and Industry Minister Shinji Sato (Monday).

STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (Monday-Friday); election of EP president (Tuesday); new EP president gives address, Irish Prime Minister John Bruton and European Commission President Santer give address on the Dublin European Council (Wednesday morning); Dutch Deputy Prime Minister Hans van Mierlo gives statement on the Dutch EU presidency (Wednesday afternoon).
BRUSSELS - Committee of the Regions holds plenary session (Wednesday-Thursday); Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio gives address (Wednesday); European Commissioner Fischler gives address (Thursday).
BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Thursday).
BRUSSELS - Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio on official visit to the Commission (Thursday).
MONDAY, JANUARY 13

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioners Brittan, van den Broek and Van Miert meet Japanese International Trade and Industry Minister Shinji Sato. Discussions will focus on the Information Technology Agreement, telecoms, EU-Japanese trade disputes.
AMSTERDAM (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Oreja attends inter-governmental conference (IGC) representatives meeting (and Tuesday).
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (first of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (1800/1700 GMT) Constitutent session: announcement of election candidates by the oldest EP deputy ("doyen d'age").
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1730/1630 GMT) Inquiry into Fraud in Transit;
Inquiry into BSE;
- (1830/1730 GMT) Institutional Affairs;
- (1900/1800 GMT) Legal Affairs.
TUESDAY, JANUARY 14
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioners Brittan and Marin meet Chile Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (second of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (1000/0900 GMT) Election of President followed by election of Vice Presidents.
- (1500/1400 GMT) (possibly) Continuation of Vice Presidential election or election of Quaestors.
WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 15
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (third of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (0900/0800 GMT) (possibly) Continuation of election of Quaestors.
- (1000/0900 GMT) Joint debate:
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton report and European Commission President Santer statement on the Dublin European Council;
- Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring statement on the Irish EU presidency including results of the WTO conference in Singapore and the situation in Serbia.
- (1230/1130 GMT) Votes on motions for resolutions on the number and membership of parliamentary committees and (possibly) continuation of election of Quaestors.

- (1500/1400 GMT) Dutch Deputy Prime Minister Hans van Mierlo statement on the Dutch EU presidency followed by debate during which Dutch State Secretary for European Affairs Michel Patijn answers questions.
- Adoption of conciliation committee texts:
- Ria Oomen-Ruijten report on long distance sales contracts;
- Dagmar Roth-Behrendt report on novel foods and ingredients;
- Karla Peijs report on cross-border transfers.
- Jan Willem Bertens report on EU/ Latin America relations: perspectives for 1996-2000 partnership strengthening.
- Carlos Carnero Gonzalez report on the renewal of the San Jose dialogue with Central America.
- Manuel Medina Ortega report on processing of personal data and protection of privacy in the telecommunications sector.
- Petrus Cornelissen report on air traffic management.
- Frits Castricum report on public service and state aids to transport.
- (1900/1800 GMT) Announcement of the proposals by the conference of presidents for appointments to committees and delegations.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1500/1400 GMT) Temporary Inquiry into BSE - European Commission President Santer gives address at 1600/1500 GMT;
- (1600/1500 GMT) Environment.
BRUSSELS - Committee of the Regions holds plenary session (first of two days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (1700/1600 GMT) Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio gives address.
- (1830/1730 GMT) Spatial planning in Europe.
- Communication on the implementation of EU regional policies in Austria, Finland and Sweden, COM(96)316.
- The global challenge of international trade: a market access strategy for the EU, COM(96)53.
- Communication from the Commission: universal service for telecoms in the perspective of a fully liberalised environment, COM(96)73.
BRUSSELS - Committee of the Regions holds forum on "Information for citizens" (and Thursday).
THURSDAY, JANUARY 16
BRUSSELS (MODIFIED ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0800 GMT).
Provisional agenda includes:
- European Commissioner Brittan communication on WTO preferential accords.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio on official visit to the Commission.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer addresses the university foundation academic session.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (fourth of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (1000/0900 GMT) Commission statement on December 19-20, 1996 Fisheries Council.
- David Thomas report on global Community strategy in the forestry sector.
- Willy De Clercq report on EU/Israel agreements on public procurement and telecoms markets.
- Winfried Menrad report on workers information and consultation.
- Ken Collins report on the protection against atmospheric pollution and forest fires.
- Diemud Theato report on the change of the legal basis to the proposal for a regulation on mutual assistance between administrations on customs and farming.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Votes on:
- Hugh Kerr report on safeguarding of workers rights in event of transfer of undertakings;
- Proposals of the President's conference and (possibly) amendments on appointments to committees and delegations;
- Motions for Dublin European Council resolutions;
- Recommendation on restrictions of marketing and use of certain hazardous substances and preparations (approximation of national legislation);
- Procedure without restrictions on marketing and use of certain hazardous substances and preparations (approximation of national legislation);
- Report without debate by Bernard Kouchner on the protocol to the fourth ACP-EC Convention of Lome following the accession of Austria, Finland and Sweden to the EU;
- Other reports under cooperation, codecision and assent procedures and on other motions for resolutions on which debate has closed.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1700/1600 GMT) Foreign Affairs;
Agriculture;
Economic;
Institutional;
- (1745/1645 GMT) Fisheries;
Energy;
External Economic Relations;
Legal;
Social Affairs;
Environment;
- (1830/1730 GMT) Transport;
Budgets;
Youth;
Development;
Civil Liberties;
- (1915/1815 GMT) Budgetary Control;
Regional Policy;
Rules of Procedure;
Women's Rights;
Petitions.
BRUSSELS - Committee of the Regions holds plenary session (second of two days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (0900/0800 GMT) European Commissioner Fischler gives address.
- (0945/0845 GMT) The CAP and eastward enlargement.
- A rural development policy.
- The role of local and regional authorities in public service, COM(96)443.

- Green paper: towards fair and efficient pricing in transport - policy options for internalising the external cost of transport in the EU. Proposal for Council directive on the charging of heavy goods vehicles for the use of certain infrastructures, COM(95)691.
- Report on the consideration of cultural aspects in European Community action, COM(96)160.
- Communication from the Commission on the review of the Community strategy for waste management, COM(96)399.
- (1430/1330 GMT) European Commissioner Oreja gives address.
- Green paper: living and working in the information society - people first, COM(96)389.
- Commission communication: learning in the information society - action plan for a European education initiative (1996-1998), COM(96)471.
- Proposal for an EP and Council decision laying down a series of guidelines on trans-European energy networks, COM(96)390.
- The role of local and regional authorities in linking education and training establishments to enterprises.

BRUSSELS - The American Chamber of Commerce (AMCHAM) and The Belgium-Japan Association and Chamber of Commerce (BJA) hold joint dinner with European Monetary Institute President Alexandre Lamfalussy on "Towards Monetary Union in 1999" (2000/1900 GMT). Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: Sheila Chabeau, AMCHAM (322) 513 6770.

AUSTRIA (NEW ITEM) - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana on official visit (and Friday); meets Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky, Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel and Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend.
FRIDAY, JANUARY 17
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer meets European Environment Bureau.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (last of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Votes on:
- Procedures without report;
- (possibly) Jutta Haug report on EC subscription to new EBRD extra shares following the decision to double the capital;
- Motions for resolutions on which debate has closed;
- (possibly) Reports under article 97;
- Helene Carrere D'Encausse report on development of EU-Transcaucasus relations;
- Giulio Fantuzzi report on the protection of geographical indications and labels of origin.
SATURDAY, JANUARY 18
No events scheduled.
SUNDAY, JANUARY 19
No events scheduled.
